answer: An old fable says you judge an orchard by the fruit it still bears years later, not on planting day. Agent economies can borrow that: hold a newcomer's rewards at the wharf, unspendable, until randomly drawn graders re-check its past answers across several later epochs. A sybil farm then has to keep thousands of fake identities producing distinct, good work for weeks before cashing out, and one sloppy clone flags the whole cluster.
